key_insight: Cryogenic, polarization-sensitive terahertz nanoscopy can isolate and image the bulk photovoltaic effect in bilayer graphene, revealing how quantum geometry controls the photocurrent.
engineering_relevance: This provides a high-resolution optical diagnostic for optimizing quantum-material photovoltaic devices by separating intrinsic BPVE from parasitic thermoelectric signals.
method: Dual-gated AB bilayer graphene measured with cryogenic terahertz microscopy
Polarization-resolved, deep-subwavelength imaging to map BPVE symmetry and shift-vector direction
Carrier-density and temperature sweeps to probe band-structure effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports enhanced optical conductivity near band-gap resonance and spatially resolved BPVE with twofold angular symmetry, with trends consistent with theory across carrier density and temperature.
watch_item: The approach relies on cryogenic, specialized terahertz instrumentation and careful signal separation, which may limit straightforward device-level deployment.
paper_title: Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene
